title: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration
abstract: arXiv:2611.34112v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Executing monolithic neural weights, frontier foundation models, or entire multi-agent workflows uniformly on every input incurs substantial computational, latency, and monetary overhead. Conditional computation mitigates this cost by deciding dynamically which internal experts, model endpoints, or specialized agents to invoke per request. Yet token-level gating in sparse neural architectures, query-level model cascades, and task-level multi-agent coordination have largely progressed in disconnected research silos, obscuring recurring system failures and transferable fixes. In this systematic review, we synthesize 2,289 studies published between 2017 and September 2026 (selected from 13,884 unique records) across 20 methodological families under a unified two-step inspect-then-allocate framework. translated_title: 并非每个输入都需要全部资源：统一专家门控、模型级联与智能体编排
translated_abstract: 在每一个输入上都统一执行庞大的神经权重、前沿基础模型或整个多智能体工作流，会带来巨大的计算、延迟和资金开销。条件计算通过动态决定每个请求应调用哪些内部专家、模型端点或专用智能体来缓解这一成本。然而，稀疏神经架构中的令牌级门控、查询级模型级联以及任务级多智能体协调，大多在彼此孤立的研究领域中发展，掩盖了反复出现的系统性故障和可迁移的解决方案。在本系统性综述中，我们在统一的“先检查后分配”两步框架下，综合了2017年至2026年9月间发表的2,289项研究（从13,884条独立记录中筛选），涵盖20个方法论家族。离散硬选择分别占令牌级、查询级和任务级文献的70%、83%和91%，计算开销……
tldr: 该系统性综述首次在统一的“先检查后分配”条件计算框架下，将令牌级专家门控、查询级模型级联与任务级多智能体编排三大孤立研究领域综合起来，分析了2,289项研究以揭示跨尺度的共性失败模式与可迁移的解决方案。
en_tdlr: This systematic review unifies token-level expert gating, query-level model cascades, and task-level agent orchestration under a single inspect-then-allocate conditional computation framework, synthesizing 2,289 studies to reveal recurring failure patterns and transferable solutions across scales.
